You will partner closely with product and engineering teams to pilot and scale AI solutions, own the operational transformation plan needed to embed AI into day-to-day field workflows, and establish the governance framework that keeps AI adoption safe, compliant, and aligned with company standards. This is a hands-on role for someone who can move from strategy to execution without heavy oversight.</p> <p>This role reports to the Vice President, Enablement & AI.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li><strong>AI Enablement Roadmap:</strong> Own and continuously evolve the roadmap for AI-driven enablement initiatives, prioritizing based on field impact, feasibility, and alignment with broader Enterprise AI team and strategy..</li> <li><strong>AI Field Use Cases:</strong> Identify, scope, and execute on high-value AI use cases for the field (e.g., deal support, prospecting, content generation, guided selling, skills, change management), working with stakeholders to define success criteria and measure impact.</li> <li><strong>AI Field Champions: </strong>build relationships with champions in the field organization to activate power-usage and drive peer-led adoption; track this adoption (e.g., usage, proficiency, behavior change) with our AI Ops Specialist and Enablement Analyst.</li> </ul> <ul> <li><strong>Ops Transformation Plan:</strong> Design and drive the operational plan that turns AI pilots into scaled, repeatable processes, coordinating across enablement, ops, and technical teams to remove execution bottlenecks.</li> <li><strong>AI Governance:</strong> Influence and lead governance standards for AI tool adoption in the field, including data usage, risk review, tool vetting, and alignment with company-wide AI policy.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Mid-Senior Experience:</strong> Several years of experience in enablement, sales operations, or a related GTM function, with a track record of owning initiatives end-to-end.</li> <li><strong>AI Solutions Experience:</strong> Direct experience evaluating, piloting, or deploying AI tools or solutions in a business context, with a solid technical understanding of how they work and where they add value. Act as the field's primary advocate for AI tools (e.g., AI-assisted prospecting, call intelligence, forecasting copilots, RFP/proposal generation).</li> <li><strong>Cross-Functional Fluency:</strong> Proven ability to work closely with product and engineering teams, translating field needs into technical requirements and vice versa.</li> <li><strong>Self-Sufficiency:</strong> Comfortable operating with significant autonomy — able to define scope, structure ambiguous problems, and drive work forward without needing detailed direction.</li> <li><strong>Organization & Execution:</strong> Strong project management instincts; able to manage multiple workstreams (roadmap, use cases, ops transformation, governance) in parallel without dropping details.</li> <li><strong>Innovative Mindset:</strong> A builder's orientation toward new technology — curious about what's possible, willing to experiment, and able to separate genuine opportunity from hype.</li> <li><strong>Enablement/Sales Background:</strong> Familiarity with field or sales enablement motions (onboarding, tool adoption, content, coaching) and how AI can realistically augment them.</li> <li><strong>GitLab Values Alignment:</strong> Ability to work in an all-remote, asynchronous environment, leaning heavily on transparency and collaboration as defined in the GitLab Handbook.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The Enablement & AI function is part of the CRO organization. Enablement is instrumental in helping GitLab grow at a more accelerated pace and achieve our ambitious revenue targets. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. title: AI Transformation Owner, Product & Design
location: Remote, Canada; Remote, United Kingdom; Remote, United States
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As an AI Transformation Owner at GitLab, you'll shape your function's AI strategy and build the solutions that deliver it. You are the person responsible for identifying where AI can fundamentally change how your org operates, partnering with your Executive Sponsor to align on the biggest challenges, and driving measurable outcomes against them.</p> <p>Think of this as a product management role where the product is your org's way of working. You'll manage the full lifecycle: understanding how work flows today, deciding where AI should reshape it, prioritizing what gets built and in what order, and ensuring what ships actually gets adopted. You'll also prototype solutions, configure agents, and prove what's possible before pulling in engineering support to scale it.</p> <p>You will work closely with an AI Engineer who sits within the Enterprise AI team. Together you form a partnership: you bring the business context, process intelligence, and strategic prioritization. They bring the technical depth, production-grade delivery, and architecture decisions. You'll build working solutions at the no-code and low-code layer, and partner with the AI Engineer on the right approach, tooling, and structure.</p> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <h3>Strategy & Prioritization</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Own your function's AI strategy,</strong> aligned with your Executive Sponsor and business priorities. Understand which metrics matter to the org, identify what will move the needle, define how you'll measure impact, and track progress over time.</li> <li><strong>Map how work flows</strong> across your function end-to-end, including the handoffs upstream and downstream to other orgs. Identify where the real constraints are, not just the ones your team can see. Focus on the 100x problems: where could leveraging AI in a workflow let your org execute it orders of magnitude faster, or at 100x more volume than before?</li> <li><strong>Manage intake</strong> of AI requests, ideas, and pain points from across the function, including via your Champion network. Ensure every team member has a clear route to surface what they need, rather than building independently.</li> <li><strong>Prioritize strategically</strong> against business outcomes and executive guidance. Hold the line on priorities - we cannot change direction every two weeks - and ensure the AI Engineer's time is spent on the highest-impact work.</li> </ul> <h3>Adoption & Change Management</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Reimagine, not just automate.</strong> Challenge your org to think beyond injecting AI into existing workflows. Work with Enterprise AI to spot opportunities to fundamentally rethink how work gets done.</li> <li><strong>Drive adoption and change management</strong> together with the AI Engineer. The best AI solution is worthless if nobody uses it. Create the channels, rituals, and feedback loops that make AI visible in your function: shared spaces for teams to show what they've built, regular office hours, onboarding for new hires, and celebration of wins. Own the rollout and iteration needed to make AI initiatives stick.</li> <li><strong>Coordinate with Enterprise AI</strong> to ensure your function benefits from patterns, tools, and learnings emerging across other parts of the business.</li> <li><strong>Build and bridge the Champion network in your function.</strong> Champions are the peer community that extends your reach beyond what you and the AI Engineer can deliver directly. From early in the role, identify and recruit Champions across sub-teams (5-10% time, formally agreed with their manager), run a regular Champion sync, host demos to the wider function, and act as their bridge to Enterprise AI. Champions are not your reports: you coordinate them, you don't manage them. Without this network, your reach is capped.</li> </ul> <h3>Hands-On Building & Agent Operations</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Build AI agents</strong> using no-code and low-code platforms (e.g. Glean, Workato, similar tools). Go from idea to working prototype without waiting for engineering.</li> <li><strong>Author and iterate on skills files</strong> that define how AI agents behave. Refine instructions based on real usage and share reusable skills across the function.</li> <li><strong>Configure MCP servers and tools,</strong> giving agents access to the business systems they need. Partner with the AI Engineer on what to connect and how to do it securely.</li> <li><strong>Own your function's fleet of agents.</strong> Some agents will be used directly by people in your org. Those that aren't, you own. Either way, you're accountable for their performance: tracking KPIs, running evaluations after model or data changes, and iterating based on what you learn.</li> <li><strong>Expect to rebuild.</strong> AI tools and models evolve fast. The agent you built last month may need to be replaced, not patched. You should be comfortable sunsetting your own work when a better approach emerges, and helping your org stay current rather than attached to what exists today.</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <h3>Business & Strategic</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Deep knowledge of your function's operations.</strong> You understand how work moves through your org, where it gets stuck, and why. You can trace a process end-to-end and explain how it connects to the teams around it.</li> <li><strong>Strategic prioritization skills.</strong> You've managed competing demands before and can make hard calls about what matters most. You think in terms of business outcomes, not activity.</li> <li><strong>A product management mindset.</strong> You naturally think about intake, backlog, iteration, and adoption. You're comfortable defining success metrics and holding yourself accountable to them.</li> <li><strong>Strong communication and influence.</strong> You'll be the person saying "not yet" to some teams and "think bigger" to others. You need the credibility and interpersonal skills to make both of those conversations land.</li> <li><strong>Cross-functional instincts.</strong> You default to understanding how your org's processes affect and are affected by the teams around you - not just optimising in isolation.</li> <li><strong>Experience building peer networks or communities of practice.</strong> You've recruited and sustained volunteer contributors before, whether as a guild lead, champion program owner, or community organizer. You know how to motivate people whose time you don't directly own.</li> </ul> <h3>Hands-On & Technical</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Comfortable building with AI tools.</strong> You don't need to write production code, but you should be able to build a working agent, configure a skill, connect an MCP server, and troubleshoot when something isn't working. Think: power user, not software engineer.</li> <li><strong>Ready to learn fast.</strong> Experience with or willingness to quickly pick up no-code/low-code AI platforms, prompt engineering, and agent configuration. You'll be trained on GitLab's specific tooling, but you should arrive ready to get your hands dirty.</li> <li><strong>Strong conceptual understanding of AI capabilities</strong> - summarization, classification, generation, automation, agentic workflows - and a commitment to staying current. The landscape shifts constantly. The tools you use today may be obsolete in weeks. You stay on top of new developments so that your org's AI strategy reflects what's actually possible, not what was possible six months ago.</li> <li><strong>Ability to map data flows</strong> - structured and unstructured. Understand where agents need context, and figure out where humans should interface with automated workflows and at what steps.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>You will partner closely with Enterprise AI within the Enterprise Technology & AI organization, while remaining embedded in your own function. Enterprise AI provides the technical delivery capability, platforms, and patterns. You provide the business context, prioritization, building at the no-code layer, and adoption muscle. Together, you form the core of your function's AI transformation.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. GitLab’s AI-powered DevSecOps platform to Mid-Market prospects and customers, tailoring messaging to their business and technical needs.</li> <li>Build and maintain a healthy pipeline through In your first year, success looks like driving customer outcomes through technical workshops and architecture guidance, developing trusted relationships with key stakeholders, increasing adoption of the GitLab platform, and strengthening retention, growth, and customer satisfaction across your portfolio. </p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Lead structured Accelerator programs from discovery through measurement, including defining outcomes, establishing baselines, creating milestones, managing the customer collaboration backlog, and documenting results.</li> <li>Guide Product Management, Sales, and Professional Services.</li> <li>Design and deliver structured technical enablement programs, including discovery workshops, custom workshops, and asynchronous guidance, while maintaining clear boundaries between Customer Success advisory work and Professional Services implementation.</li> <li>Support and lead account escalations by coordinating technical context, follow-up actions, customer communications, and clear exit criteria.</li> <li>Analyze GitLab usage, adoption, and maturity signals to identify risks, prioritize interventions, and recommend next steps.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Practical understanding of Git, common branching strategies, and modern software development lifecycles.</li> <li>Working knowledge of continuous integration, continuous deployment, and DevSecOps practices.</li> <li>Experience guiding customers through technical or architectural decisions in complex enterprise environments.</li> <li>Experience facilitating technical workshops, enablement programs, and structured customer adoption initiatives.</li> <li>Experience partnering with customers to define business outcomes and translate them into actionable success plans, key goals, and measures.</li> <li>Background in customer success, post-sales, or professional services roles focused on adoption, retention, and satisfaction.</li> <li>Ability to manage a portfolio of customers, including handling escalations and coordinating across Support, Product Management, Sales, and Professional Services.</li> <li>Strong communication, presentation, and organizational skills, with attention to detail and analytical thinking.</li> <li>Experience planning and managing projects or initiatives in technical environments, including identifying training and enablement needs.</li> <li>Alignment with GitLab’s values and interest in applying transferable skills from related roles or industries, with flexibility to travel as needed according to company policy.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>We are part of GitLab’s Customer Success organization. You will independently lead complex employment law matters end-to-end, including representing GitLab before works councils and labor courts, as well as setting the strategy for managing employment risk in the region. and cross-functional partners.</p> <h3>What you’ll do</h3> <ul> <li>Provide senior, practical employment-law advice to team members and stakeholders across GitLab, balancing legal risk, business objectives, and GitLab’s values, serving as a subject-matter resource for legal colleagues and cross-functional partners.</li> <li>Directly manage matters across the employment lifecycle, including recruiting and onboarding, compensation, performance management, leave management, employee relations, works council processes, organizational changes, separation, and post-employment issues.</li> <li>Directly negotiate and engage with works councils and employee representative bodies across EMEA jurisdictions, and lead consultation processes for organizational change.</li> <li>Represent GitLab in, or directly manage outside counsel appearances for, labor courts, employment tribunals, and agency investigations, including case strategy, fact development, witness preparation, and settlement decisions.</li> <li>Counsel People Business Partners, Team Member Relations partners, and business leaders on complex and sensitive team-member relations concerns.</li> <li>Draft, review, negotiate, and maintain employment agreements, separation agreements, policies, templates, and related documentation across multiple jurisdictions.</li> <li>Own employment compliance across EMEA and incorporate outside-counsel input into strategies that match the business.</li> <li>Monitor and analyze changes in employment, privacy, and related laws; identify legal risks; and translate developments into practical recommendations and implementable guidance.</li> <li>Lead the development and continuous improvement of scalable employment-law processes, systems, playbooks, templates, and supporting documentation for the Legal and People teams.</li> <li>Provide employment advice in regions outside EMEA as needed.</li> <li>Use GitLab to collaborate transparently and work effectively in an asynchronous, globally distributed environment.<br><br></li> </ul> <h3>What you’ll bring</h3> <ul> <li>A Juris Doctor (JD), Bachelor of Laws (LLB), or local equivalent, admitted to practice in at least one EMEA jurisdiction.</li> <li>Substantial, firsthand experience advising a multinational company with works councils across EMEA, including direct hands-on negotiation and consultation experience.</li> <li>A demonstrated track record of advocating or managing outside counsel in labor courts, employment tribunals and analogous proceedings .</li> <li>Deep knowledge of employment compliance requirements across EMEA, with the judgment to identify when advice from local counsel is needed.</li> <li>Experience counseling People Business Partners, Team Member Relations partners, and business leaders on sensitive and complex employment matters, including works council strategy.</li> <li>Experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating employment agreements, separation agreements, policies, templates, and related documentation across multiple jurisdictions.</li> <li>Fluency with GDPR and other local privacy requirements related to team-member data.</li> <li>Experience building or significantly improving legal processes, systems, playbooks, templates, and documentation that produce consistent outcomes at scale.</li> <li>Strong issue-spotting, risk-assessment, and judgment skills, with the ability to provide clear recommendations and practical solutions.</li> <li>The ability to manage a high volume of complex legal matters independently and business.</li> <li>A practical and creative approach to problem-solving, sound business judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to work across functions, time zones, and cultures.</li> <li>Comfort working in a remote, globally distributed, asynchronous environment; willingness to learn and use GitLab in your day-to-day work.<br><br></li> </ul> <h3>About The Team</h3> <p>The issues, merge requests, and the GitLab handbook.</li> </ul> <h4>What you’ll bring</h4> <ul> <li value="1"><span class="textBold">Experience leading</span> engineering organizations with multiple teams Software Composition Analysis, secret detection, vulnerability management workflows, and software supply chain security.</li> <li value="3"><span class="textBold">Experience building</span> detection, analysis, or scanning systems in a software as a service or DevSecOps environment, including trade-offs across precision, recall, latency, and scale.</li> <li value="4"><span class="textBold">Direct experience shipping</span> a customer-facing AI or machine learning product feature tied to detection or remediation quality outcomes.</li> <li value="5"><span class="textBold">Ability to partner</span> closely with product management on roadmap planning, prioritization, and requirements in a product-led context.</li> <li value="6"><span class="textBold">Strong written communication Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As Director, Product Management: Agentic Software Delivery, you'll own one of GitLab's most strategic sections, spanning Continuous Integration, Artifact Management, Continuous Deployment, and Observability. You'll lead senior and principal product managers and be accountable for adoption, retention, and revenue across build, package, deploy, and monitor. Today, these are separate stages with a human making the call at each handoff. As agents take on more coding, pipeline, and deployment work, you'll set the three-year vision for how much of that judgment the system can make safely and how quickly a production signal can turn into a fix without waiting for a human to notice it first. You'll define how customers move from today's manual checkpoints toward agent-driven software delivery at a pace that fits their risk tolerance. In your first year, you'll bring four connected roadmaps into one coherent strategy, establish how investment is allocated and reallocated, deepen partnerships with Engineering and go-to-market leaders, and give customers a credible path for managing software delivery at scale.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Own the strategy, three-year vision, and business outcomes for GitLab's Agentic Software Delivery section, with a clear point of view on how artificial intelligence is changing software delivery.</li> <li value="2">Lead and develop senior and principal product managers across Continuous Integration, Artifact Management, Continuous Deployment, and Observability, helping them grow as independent decision-makers.</li> <li value="3">Establish the frameworks, standards, and operating rhythm that support consistent, high-quality product decisions without unnecessary escalation.</li> <li value="4">Own section-level key performance indicators and adoption funnels, using the results to reallocate investment or stop work that isn't paying off.</li> <li value="5">Evaluate major strategic bets, partnerships, and build, buy, or partner decisions, and develop the business cases that support them.</li> <li value="6">Partner with Engineering leadership on platform investment, architectural direction, and trade-offs across the section, while connecting build, package, deploy, and monitor into one coherent customer experience.</li> <li value="7">Drive pricing, packaging, go-to-market strategy, migration, and adoption with Product Marketing, Sales, Pricing, Customer Success, and Solutions Engineering across free, commercial, and enterprise offerings.</li> <li value="8">Represent the section with GitLab's senior leadership, key enterprise customers, partners, and industry audiences, while modeling AI-native product management across discovery, synthesis, prototyping, roadmap exploration, and concept development.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Experience leading product managers, including developing senior and principal talent, hiring, and addressing performance directly.</li> <li value="2">A track record of owning a portfolio across multiple product areas and being accountable for adoption, retention, and revenue, not only roadmap delivery.</li> <li value="3">Product management depth in one or more relevant areas, such as continuous integration and continuous delivery pipelines, artifact or package management, release management, or observability.</li> <li value="4">Sound judgment about where to invest and where to stop, including experience making and defending build, buy, or partner decisions with a business case.</li> <li value="5">Technical fluency to work with engineers and architects on pipeline design, artifact workflows, deployment strategies, and observability signals such as logs, metrics, and traces.</li> <li value="6">Experience shaping pricing and packaging for technical products across free, commercial, and enterprise offerings.</li> <li value="7">Experience working with technical customers in developer tools, DevOps, or software delivery environments where engineers and engineering leaders are primary users.</li> <li value="8">Executive-level communication and influence.</li> <li value="9">Practical use of AI tools in product management workflows, along with a thoughtful view of how AI and agentic workflows are changing software delivery. We welcome candidates whose experience may come from different but transferable product and leadership paths.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The team brings together senior product leaders across GitLab's software delivery platform and works closely with Engineering, Design, and go-to-market partners so customers experience these capabilities as one connected system. The team helps customers manage today's delivery complexity while shaping how AI-powered and AI-native workflows influence the next generation of software delivery. As part of GitLab's all-remote organization, the team collaborates asynchronously across regions with a focus on transparency, written communication, and clear decision-making.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. talent goals.</li> <li>Guide content planning and publishing across social channels while maintaining a consistent GitLab voice.</li> <li>Own the social media budget, tooling stack, and agency, description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h3>An overview of this role</h3> <p>As the Director, Strategic Partnerships, you will own GitLab's relationships with its two major cloud infrastructure partners: AWS and Google Cloud. This is a single-threaded owner role, reporting to the VP, Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships. You will shape partnership strategy from the top down and drive execution from the ground up, this is as much about running the weekly grind of a partnership as it is about setting its direction, turning strategic relationships into durable business outcomes.</p> <p>You will own the commercial relationship end-to-end: managing GitLab's cloud infrastructure spend and consumption commitments, and leading renewal negotiations for enterprise agreements (e.g., EDPs, MACCs, or equivalent) before they come due. You will also own the technical and go-to-market side of each relationship: driving product integrations, shaping joint go-to-market strategy, and connecting GitLab's product roadmap and AI strategy to concrete partner initiatives. This is not a co-sell, channel, or revenue-through-partners role. Success here looks like disciplined commercial ownership, technical integration depth, and renewal outcomes that protect and grow GitLab's position, not partner-sourced pipeline or quota attainment.</p> <p>This role sits close to GitLab's evolving AI strategy and the future of our AI-powered DevSecOps platform. You will develop a clear point of view, represent these partnerships with senior stakeholders, and personally drive the day-to-day work that spans multi-year planning and weekly execution, chasing down blockers, keeping workstreams on track, and doing the detailed follow-through yourself rather than delegating it.</p> <h3>What you'll do</h3> <ul> <li>Serve as the primary owner and point of contact for GitLab's cloud infrastructure partnerships with AWS and Google Cloud, personally accountable for the direction, operating rhythm, and outcomes of each.</li> <li>Own the full commercial lifecycle of each relationship: negotiating rates and terms, tracking consumption against committed spend, and leading renewal negotiations well ahead of contract expiration.</li> <li>Manage cloud infrastructure spend as a standing responsibility, partnering with Finance/FinOps on forecasting, true-ups, and cost optimization across both hyperscalers.</li> <li>Drive product integrations with each partner, working directly with engineering and product management counterparts on both sides to identify, scope, and deliver joint technical initiatives.</li> <li>Develop and lead joint go-to-market strategy for each partnership, connecting GitLab's business priorities, product roadmap, and AI strategy to concrete partner initiatives, and then own getting those plans executed.</li> <li>Build strong working relationships across partner organizations, including executives, product management, engineering, sales, and marketing stakeholders.</li> <li>Run a disciplined operating cadence across complex initiatives, with clear priorities, owners, timelines, coordination points, and follow-through you drive yourself.</li> <li>Coordinate cross-functional work inside GitLab to support partnership goals, aligning teams across product, engineering, sales, marketing, finance, and the executive group.</li> <li>Translate partner opportunities and requests into actionable internal plans, including roadmap discussions, integration needs, commercial terms, and executive recommendations.</li> <li>Track and communicate measurable partnership outcomes such as spend efficiency, consumption trends, renewal terms secured, integration progress, and joint go-to-market execution.</li> <li>Represent the partnerships at the executive level by preparing clear recommendations, briefing executives, and helping drive alignment on investments, trade-offs, and next steps.</li> </ul> <h3>What you'll bring</h3> <ul> <li>Significant experience owning strategic partnerships, alliance relationships, or vendor/commercial relationships in enterprise software, cloud, and/or AI, with a track record of being in the details, not just setting direction. This experience should reflect owning one or a small number of relationships in depth, not administering a large multi-partner channel ecosystem.</li> <li>Direct experience managing enterprise cloud commercial agreements (e.g., EDP, MACC, or similar consumption/spend commitments) with at least one major hyperscaler, including experience owning a renewal cycle from expiration planning through negotiation and close.</li> <li>Experience driving product or technical integrations with a cloud partner, and shaping joint go-to-market strategy that connects a product roadmap to partner initiatives.</li> <li>Strong ownership mindset with the ability to operate as a single-threaded owner who is accountable for both strategy and execution, and comfortable doing the hands-on work personally rather than handing it off.</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex commercial and partnership topics into clear recommendations for executives and cross-functional stakeholders.</li> <li>Strong project and program management skills, including the ability to organize complex workstreams, prioritize effectively, and keep multiple initiatives moving through direct, hands-on management.</li> <li>Genuine technical fluency in software development, platform integrations, and cloud infrastructure, with comfort engaging engineering and product counterparts in substantive conversations, not just positioning technology commercially.</li> <li>Experience working with senior stakeholders on high-visibility initiatives, including preparing executive briefings, framing recommendations, and driving follow-through.</li> <li>Ability to influence without formal authority, build strong working relationships across internal and external teams, and navigate multiple priorities with sound judgment.</li> <li>Familiarity with the DevSecOps ecosystem and a results-oriented approach to measuring partnership impact through spend efficiency and business/product outcomes rather than partner-sourced revenue or quota attainment.</li> <li>Preferred: candidates based in US Eastern or Central time zones, given close cross-functional coordination needs.</li> </ul> <h3>About the team</h3> <p>The Strategic Partnerships team owns the strategy and relationship management for some of GitLab's most consequential external partners, including the hyperscalers powering GitLab's infrastructure and future AI capabilities. We work across product, engineering, sales, marketing, finance, and the executive group to turn these partnerships into differentiated value for GitLab, manage our infrastructure investment responsibly, and ensure these relationships support our long-term platform strategy.</p> <p> </p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. They carry years of accumulated architectural decisions, they sit in the critical path of our customers' own delivery pipelines, and they are being reshaped by the shift toward AI native development. Core DevOps is where much of that strategy has to land, because these are the services our own engineers and our customers depend on daily. In this role you will bring that strategy into Core DevOps in a form that works for long lived production systems, and carry what you learn here back out to the rest of engineering.</p> <p><strong>What You'll Do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Set and continuously refine the go forward technical direction for CI, CD, Plan, and source code experiences, aligned against the horizontal architectural initiatives.</li> <li>Work directly with the VP of Engineering as her technical counterpart on planning, technical investment, and where the group's engineering effort should go.</li> <li>Translate GitLab's company-wide productivity, quality, and AI native engineering goals into concrete technical direction for Core DevOps, and turn into iterable roadmaps, partnering broadly across the org.</li> <li>Define what good means in measurable terms for these services, including availability, latency at p95 and p99, pipeline success rate, test reliability, data correctness, and defect escape rate, then hold designs and implementations to it.</li> <li>Maintain a clear and current picture of systemic technical risk across the group, including single points of failure, unowned critical paths, brittle coupling between CI/CD and Plan, scaling limits, and past decisions that now constrain the roadmap. Drive a prioritized plan to retire it.</li> <li>Lead the hardest design decisions hands on, writing code, prototypes, and proofs of concept where a design argument needs evidence behind it.</li> <li>Drive convergence on shared patterns, libraries, and paved paths, reducing how many different ways the same problem gets solved across the group.</li> <li>Design migration paths that let large, long lived systems change underneath users without breaking them, using incremental cutover, dual run, measurable rollback, and deprecation with clear timelines.</li> <li>Adopt the platform capabilities coming from GitLab's AI organization and the company's productivity initiatives into Core DevOps, feed this group's requirements back into them, and help prove what works on systems of this scale and maturity.</li> <li>Serve as the escalation point for complex or contested technical decisions across the group, including those where no single team owns the outcome.</li> <li>Review significant designs and merge requests in the group's critical paths, and use review to teach rather than only to gate.</li> <li>Ensure designs hold across GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and Self-Managed deployments, and respect multi-tenant, compliance, and data governance boundaries in each.</li> <li>Partner with Infrastructure, Security, and SRE so Core DevOps services are observable and debuggable, and so failure modes degrade gracefully instead of cascading.</li> <li>Make architectural constraints and opportunities clear to Product in roadmap terms, so that technical investment and product ambition get planned together instead of traded off late.</li> <li>Write clear, opinionated design documents, architecture narratives, and decision records that let teams across the group make aligned decisions independently.</li> <li>Grow Principal and Staff Engineers across Core DevOps, raise the bar on design rigor and technical writing, and contribute to the technical hiring bar for senior individual contributors.</li> <li>Participate in the Incident Management on-call rotation to help meet availability goals for GitLab.com, and complete Interview Training to participate in hiring as a technical interviewer or panel member.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You'll Bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>10+ years of software engineering experience, including 4+ years in a Staff, Principal, or equivalent senior technical leadership role.</li> <li>Deep expertise in AI and ML systems, including large language models, agentic frameworks, and autonomous workflow design at production scale.</li> <li>Proven track record of leading hands-on technical experimentation, including defining evaluation frameworks, running benchmarks, and translating findings into scalable architecture decisions.</li> <li>Strong background in scalable, multi-tenant distributed systems, including service decomposition, fault tolerance, observability, and operational resilience.</li> <li>Experience designing and implementing human-in-the-loop controls, safety guardrails, and responsible AI practices for production systems.</li> <li>Experience mentoring senior engineers and influencing technical direction across multiple teams or divisions without direct authority.</li> <li>Ability to work effectively in a fully remote, globally distributed organization with excellent written and asynchronous description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <p>As Engineering Manager at GitLab, you’ll manage and grow a high-performing engineering team within the Data Foundations group, working on a core data platform that ingests, processes, persists, and queries data streams generated across GitLab.</p> <p>We are looking for a leader who can leverage AI to drive non-linear productivity gains across the platform, accelerating our ability to deliver value to our customers.</p> <p>We’re looking for someone with deep distributed systems knowledge. You’ll need to be comfortable going well beyond people management and into the architecture of high-throughput, multi-component data systems: ingestion, buffering, enrichment, replication, storage, querying, backpressure handling, isolation, and production operations across multiple deployment models.</p> <p>You’ll partner closely with Product, Design, Infrastructure, Data, and other Engineering teams to evolve a platform that lives inside the product, keeps external services to a minimum, and runs across GitLab.com, Dedicated, Self-Managed, and Cells-based deployments.</p> <p>In addition to Data Insights Platform, this role will take on classic search scope as the team joins the Data Foundations organization. You’ll help lead architecture and execution across both GitLab’s analytics platform and classic search capabilities, balancing platform depth with customer-facing impact.</p> <p>You’ll help lead architecture and execution across both GitLab’s analytics platform and classic search capabilities, balancing platform depth with customer-facing impact.</p> <p>In this role, you’ll balance technical guidance with people management. You’ll hire, coach, and develop engineers while also helping drive architecture and execution across a platform built around stateless ingesters, Siphon CDC replication, NATS/JetStream buffering, enrichment pipelines, ClickHouse-backed storage, and a Query API that interfaces with the GitLab Rails monolith.</p> <p>In Data Foundations, we build the engineering systems that make platform data reliable, scalable, and available to product teams across GitLab, and you’ll help guide that work.</p> <h4><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h4> <ul> <li> <p>Hire, manage, and enable a high-performing Data Insights Platform engineering team, creating an environment where team members can do their best work and deliver strong results.</p> </li> <li> <p>Partner closely with product managers, product designers, and peer engineering managers to define and deliver the roadmap for <a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/analytics-section/platform-insights/core/">Data Insights Platform</a> (DIP) and related Platform Insights initiatives such as <a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/analytics-section/siphonhttps://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/analytics-section/siphon">Siphon</a>, Query API integrations, classic search initiatives, and self-service reporting foundations.</p> </li> <li> <p>Own delivery for your team, including planning, prioritization, execution, and operational follow-through across architecture work, platform improvements, and production readiness, with clear accountability for roadmap milestones and delivery outcomes.</p> </li> <li> <p>Guide the technical design of distributed data-path components, including ingestion, buffering, enrichment, exporting, and querying, and shape architecture choices on sharding, partitioning, component-specific scaling, failure recovery, and tenant isolation across SaaS, Dedicated, self-managed, and Cells deployments, with a strong focus on reliability, throughput, operability, and maintainability.</p> </li> <li> <p>Help the team design safe and scalable integrations with the GitLab monolith, including gRPC/Protobuf-based query paths and clear ownership boundaries between DIP and product teams building user-facing GraphQL or REST endpoints.</p> </li> <li> <p>Drive a high bar for security, privacy, and governance in how platform data is handled, including authentication, authorization, encryption, and safe handling of data with different privacy classifications.</p> </li> <li> <p>Improve operational maturity across the platform, including observability, metrics, logging, readiness, capacity planning, performance monitoring, and clear runbooks for managed environments, with a focus on improving availability, throughput, latency, and time to recovery.</p> </li> <li> <p>Collaborate asynchronously across teams and functions to help GitLab land customer-facing reporting capabilities on top of a strong, scalable data foundation.</p> </li> <li> <p>Lead the design and evolution of the platform with a focus on modular architecture, ensuring systems are extensible and ready for AI-driven integrations.</p> </li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li> <p>Experience managing platform, infrastructure, or data systems teams at scale, with a track record of building high-performing, values-aligned teams.</p> </li> <li> <p>Deep distributed systems expertise, including strong judgment on service boundaries, asynchronous pipelines, backpressure, fault tolerance, horizontal scalability, and operating multi-component systems in production.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong technical background in backend and platform engineering, with the ability to guide architecture for high-throughput event pipelines and data systems.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience with technologies and patterns relevant to this space, such as change data capture, event streaming or messaging systems, OLAP data stores, query-serving layers, and service-to-service APIs.</p> </li> <li> <p>Ability to hire, develop, and coach team members while still contributing technical guidance on complex architecture and delivery tradeoffs.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, especially when ownership is split between platform teams and feature teams consuming common infrastructure or APIs.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience building or operating systems across multiple deployment models, with sound judgment about the tradeoffs between GitLab.com, Dedicated, self-managed, and cell-based environments.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong written communication skills and the ability to work effectively in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.</p> </li> <li> <p>Familiarity with search, indexing, and query-serving systems is a strong plus.</p> </li> <li> <p>A deep passion for reliability, customer outcomes, and engineering and operational excellence, with a proven track record of instilling these values in high-performing teams.</p> </li> </ul> <h4><strong>About the team</strong></h4> <p>In Data Foundations, we enable customers to self-serve reporting with scalable architecture. Our vision is to build a comprehensive dashboards-as-a-service framework that uses AI and relies on scalable data infrastructure.</p> <p>Data Insights Platform is one of our central initiatives, and we play a key role in advancing self-service reporting across GitLab. This is the foundational layer every reporting and intelligence surface at GitLab depends on — from product dashboards to Software Engineering Intelligence to the GitLab Knowledge Graph.</p> <p>In addition to Data Insights Platform, the team’s scope will include classic search as part of the broader Data Foundations organization.This brings together foundational analytics and search capabilities that help customers generate insights from product data and find relevant information across GitLab.</p> <p>We partner closely with product teams to turn DIP’s real-time insights, Postgres-to-ClickHouse replication, event routing, and downstream exports into dashboards, agent experiences, and customer-facing reporting.</p> <p>The scale expectations are real: we handle very large event volumes, with current and projected usage in the hundreds of millions of events per day.</p> <p>For more on how we work, see:</p> <ul> <li> <p><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/analytics/platform-insights/">Platform Insights Group</a></p> </li> <li> <p><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/architecture/design-documents/data_insights_platform/">Data Insights Platform architecture blueprint</a></p> </li> <li> <p><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/architecture/design-documents/data_insights_platform_querying_api/">Data Insights Platform Querying API</a></p> </li> </ul><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>The Trusted Agentic Development team sits within GitLab's Developer Experience group and builds the platforms our own engineers rely on every day. GitLab engineers increasingly build software with artificial intelligence (AI) agents. Agents generate code and tests in seconds, so speed is no longer the constraint. Confidence is. Agents can produce a passing test suite for software that doesn't work as intended, and a reviewer may not be able to tell the difference without redoing the work by hand.</p> <p>As Engineering Manager, Trusted Agentic Development, you'll build and lead the team that closes this gap. You'll help define what validation means when the author is an agent and make the feedback loop fast, automatic, and trustworthy. You'll point the team at the right version of an open problem and earn adoption across GitLab by building the best path, not by mandating a process.</p> <ul> <li value="1">Validation that confirms agent-generated code does what was intended, so a passing suite means a working feature and not just a satisfied proxy.</li> <li value="2">Mid-loop feedback that helps an agent self-correct toward working software instead of green assertions.</li> <li value="3">Language-aware approaches under one shared model of what "trusted" means, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, while allowing the right technique to differ by language.</li> <li value="4">Real measurement of whether engineers trust and adopt the path, with findings fed directly back into the platform.</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Build and grow the team by hiring and developing engineers who practice agentic development, and create a culture that treats this as an open problem to solve rather than a process to enforce.</li> <li value="2">Set direction in an undefined space by partnering with your team to shape the technical approach for validating agent-built software.</li> <li value="3">Keep the team focused on the highest-impact version of the problem rather than the easiest one.</li> <li value="4">Earn adoption by building relationships with engineering teams across GitLab, learning how they work with agents today, and creating a platform they choose because it makes them faster and more confident.</li> <li value="5">Measure engineer adoption and trust through real usage, treat adopters as design partners, and use findings to prioritize where confidence is breaking down.</li> <li value="6">Stay close to the technical work by engaging in architecture and design discussions, reviewing proposals, and keeping your judgment current as agentic development changes.</li> <li value="7">Run the team with clear goals, direct feedback, honest performance management, and ownership of complex work from planning through completion without relying on a dedicated program manager.</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Direct experience using AI agents to build software, including lessons from successes and missteps and a clear point of view on why a passing test suite isn't the same as working software.</li> <li value="2">Experience leading engineering teams through ambiguous, early-stage problems where the right approach wasn't yet known.</li> <li value="3">The ability to drive adoption through influence and a useful product rather than through mandate, including partnering across teams you don't manage.</li> <li value="4">Technical depth to engage credibly in architecture and validation strategy discussions and earn the trust of senior engineers.</li> <li value="5">Experience designing distributed systems designed to run on Kubernetes first.</li> <li value="5">A history of building accountable, high-performing teams, including hiring well, developing team members, and addressing underperformance directly.</li> <li value="6">Strong written communication skills in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.</li> <li value="7">Alignment with GitLab's values, especially collaboration, iteration, and transparency.</li> </ul> <p>This isn't a quality assurance (QA) or test automation management role. We care far more about your experience leading teams that build with agents than about depth in any particular testing discipline.</p> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Trusted Agentic Development team is part of GitLab's Developer Experience group. We build platforms and practices that help GitLab engineers validate agent-generated software with confidence. We work across engineering teams and programming languages to understand how people use agents, test new approaches in real workflows, and create a shared model of trusted agentic development that teams choose to adopt.</p> <p><strong><em>Poland base salary range:</em></strong><em> <strong>296,000 PLN – 444,000 PLN</strong></em><br><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the EU, applicable in the specified country or countries only. code to GitLab’s product and adjacent systems.</li> <li>Develop bug fixes, features, integrations, tooling, and performance improvements when strategic customer outcomes require direct engineering strategically important customers when adoption, retention, executive confidence, or public trust is materially at risk.</li> <li>Diagnose complex problems across GitLab product behavior, customer architecture, Git internals, CI/CD workflows, API usage, observability, infrastructure, networking, and cloud environments.</li> <li>Coordinate across Product, Engineering, SRE, Support, SA, CSA, CSM, and agentic software development lifecycle</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Drive governed, measurable, and production-oriented adoption of GitLab Duo Agent Platform with strategic customers.</li> <li>Identify and resolve AI adoption blockers involving governance, usage controls, auditability, security, compliance, operating models, workflow design, and integrations.</li> <li>Develop customer-safe adoption patterns for the agentic software development lifecycle (SDLC), AI-assisted development, intent-based review, AI governance, and human-in-the-loop software delivery.</li> <li>Partner with Product, Engineering, Field, and Customer Success teams to turn AI adoption learning into reusable guidance and product improvements.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Thought leadership</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Create technical narratives grounded in customer experience and product reality that can help shape the industry’s approach.</li> <li>Contribute to Well-Architected Frameworks, whitepapers, webinars, reference architectures, technical strategy memos, and adoption frameworks.</li> <li>Guide ideas through discovery, formulation, validation, amplification, and adoption across GitLab.</li> <li>Partner with SA, CSA, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Product Marketing Management, CSM, Support, and executive stakeholders to make technical thought leadership a shared company capability.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Staff-level experience building, operating, or improving complex production software systems.</li> <li>Experience contributing to large, mature product codebases with high standards for testing, maintainability, performance, and security.</li> <li>Strong Ruby on Rails or Go experience and the ability to contribute directly to GitLab’s product and adjacent systems.</li> <li>Experience with AI-assisted software development, agentic workflows, AI governance, model evaluation, context management, prompt and workflow design, or AI adoption in enterprise environments.</li> <li>Experience diagnosing complex system behavior across application code, data stores, infrastructure, observability, networking, APIs, and customer usage patterns.</li> strategic customers or senior technical stakeholders in ambiguous, high-impact situations.</li> <li>The ability to coordinate across product, engineering, field, and customer teams without formal authority.</li> <li>Strong written communication and sound judgment, including the ability to create technical narratives and distinguish reusable product work from customer-specific customization.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Strongly preferred qualifications</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Direct experience with GitLab as a platform, including GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, or GitLab engineering, infrastructure engineering, or distributed systems.</li> <li>Experience working in open source or highly asynchronous engineering environments.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Technologies and performance analysis</li> <li>Vue and TypeScript</li> <li>APIs and automation</li> <li>DevSecOps governance, security, and compliance</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What this role is not</strong></h2> <p>This engineering teams.</li> <li>Strengthen credential handling across hosts, including bearer tokens, session cookies, and CSRF protection.</li> <li>Optimize bundle size, startup cost, and dependency weight for browser consumers, and support a Tier 2 on-call rotation for urgent engineering issues.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Strong proficiency with TypeScript Vue.</li> <li>Experience designing APIs that other people use, with the ability to explain what you'd do differently.</li> <li>Understanding of the differences between running code in Node.js and in the browser, and how to write code that works in both.</li> <li>A security-minded development approach, including careful credential handling and performance optimization.</li> <li>Ability to communicate clearly and concisely in writing about technical problems, propose iterative solutions, and work effectively in an agile environment.</li> <li>Self-motivation, strong organizational Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>About the role</strong></h2> <p>As an Intermediate Backend Engineer, you will take backend features and improvements from clarifying the problem through shipping them and following up in production. You will work within a product area, partnering with Product Management, Frontend, Infrastructure, and Security to deliver predictably and contribute to the quality, security, performance, and maintainability of shared backend code and services. You will be trusted to work with minimal guidance, to know when to seek help, and to communicate clearly in a remote, asynchronous environment — with other tenured engineers alongside you to review your work, think through hard problems with you, and help you grow.</p> <h2><strong>Why you’ll love this role</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Ownership:</strong> You'll take features from requirements through delivery and follow-up; your code will run on a platform used by millions of users.</li> <li><strong>Learning and Growth :</strong> You’ll work alongside your engineering team, who treat code review and design review as a learning loop rather than a gate — one of the fastest ways to grow your engineering judgment.</li> <li><strong>Innovative Culture:</strong> You’ll use AI as a genuine part of daily engineering work, developing the judgment to know when to trust it and when not to.</li> <li><strong>Autonomy:</strong> You’ll thrive in our remote-first, asynchronous organization, where clear written communication and self-direction are the pillars of success.</li> <li><strong>User-Centric Collaboration:</strong> You’ll partner closely with PMs and designers to shape requirements, so you understand why you’re building something, not just what.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Own and Ship Features:</strong> Design, implement, test, and ship backend features and improvements with minimal guidance, working in Ruby/Rails, Go, or any other modern languages.</li> <li><strong>Build for Production:</strong> Write maintainable, secure, observable, and performant code. Design and maintain APIs, background jobs, integrations, and bounded service functionality, and work with data models, migrations, indexes, and query behavior.</li> <li><strong>Test and Review:</strong> Add and improve automated coverage — unit, integration, contract, and end-to-end where appropriate — and review others’ code for correctness, maintainability, security, performance, and operational risk.</li> <li><strong>Operate What You Build:</strong> Investigate build, test, deployment, and runtime failures at the feature boundary, identify technical debt and propose practical improvements, and take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.</li> <li><strong>Leverage AI:</strong> Use AI productively in daily work, validate what it produces, and understand where its limitations matter.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Backend Fundamentals:</strong> Professional experience building and shipping production backend applications, with strong programming, API, database, testing, debugging, and performance fundamentals.</li> <li><strong>Adaptability:</strong> Experience with Ruby/Rails, Go, or any other modern backend language. runbooks, procedures, templates, and other documentation that make vulnerability handling more efficient and transparent.</li> <li>Participate in incident handoffs, root cause analysis documentation, lessons-learned activities, and product security reviews.</li> <li>Build technical and operational expertise in PSIRT, bug bounty, vulnerability management, and coordinated vulnerability disclosure.</li> </ul> <h4>What you’ll bring</h4> <ul> <li>Early-career experience or equivalent education in cybersecurity, software engineering, information technology, or a related field. VulnOps serves as a central point of contact for external security researchers and helps govern the policies, processes, and guidelines used to address vulnerabilities in GitLab’s supported products.</p> <p>Team members collaborate across regions using documented processes, automation, and structured handoffs to support vulnerability resolution and ongoing operational improvements.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This role operates on a compressed 4-day work schedule, with a full-time week's hours condensed into four longer working days. <strong>Shifts run Sunday through Wednesday to provide 24/7/365 security coverage.</strong></p> <p>Your primary focus will be detecting and responding to security incidents during your scheduled shifts. You'll learn to think both tactically and strategically about security, while getting hands-on experience handling real-world incidents.</p> <p>Successful Security Engineers thrive in high-pressure environments, remaining calm while following prepared runbooks and thinking critically about security challenges. In this role, you will learn to think like both an attacker and defender, developing proactive and preventative security measures to keep GitLab and its users' data safe in our ever-changing threat landscape. href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/security/security-operations/signals-engineering/"><br><br></a></li> </ul> <p><strong>What you’ll do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li>Lead security incident response in our 24/7 global rotation, managing incidents from detection through containment and recovery</li> <li>Create and maintain comprehensive incident response documentation, including runbooks and standard procedures</li> <li>Conduct post-incident analysis through RCA and lessons-learned reviews to strengthen our incident response program</li> <li>Design and implement automated security processes to improve operational efficiency and reduce manual intervention</li> <li>Drive continuous improvement by identifying security gaps and implementing advanced detection and response capabilities</li> <li>Collaborate across GitLab teams to develop new security capabilities and deliver technical projects that enhance our infrastructure</li> </ul> <p><strong>What you’ll <p>Recognize impediments to our efficiency as a team ("technical debt"), propose and implement solutions</p> </li> <li> <p>Participate in<a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/on-call/"> on-call rotations</a> to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues.</p> </li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li> <p>Experience building and maintaining backend applications with Ruby on Rails.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience delivering and maintaining software systems as part of a larger engineering team.</p> </li> <li> <p>The ability to investigate technical problems, ask for context when needed, and work toward a practical resolution.</p> </li> from others, sharing knowledge, and growing your technical skills.</p> </li> <li> <p>Frontend development experience, including JavaScript or Vue.js, is helpful.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience with Elasticsearch, graph databases, vulnerability management, application security, or related transferable skills is helpful.</p> </li> </ul> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>The Vulnerability title: Intermediate Support Engineer (SHIFT)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <h4>This is a shift role. Working 8-hour shifts with 4 weekdays and 1 weekend day.</h4> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Support Engineering at GitLab isn’t just a title - you will be embedded within the Engineering department and will truly operate in an environment where Support and Engineering meet. You’ll interact with customers daily as they encounter the difficult edge cases of running GitLab in complex environments. In the space of a day, you might be doing behind the scenes work of a Linux administrator troubleshooting performance problems by using strace on a particular process, interacting with the Product team to ensure that steps in a bug report are reproducible, or interacting with the Engineering team itself by diving deep into our codebase and putting together a merge request to actually fix a customer issue. </span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">That’s not all though - you’d equally be invited to contribute to the source code, improve our documentation, and help build out more efficient support processes in our issue tracker. We want to live in a world where everyone can contribute, and as a member of the support team, there are no barriers to using your skills to improve the experience of our users and customers.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><br></span><span style="font-weight: 400;"> Some examples of our projects: </span></p> <ul> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/gitlab-detective">A tool to automatically check a GitLab Omnibus install for known issues</a></li> <li>A<a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/gitlabsos"> solution to capture the state of a customer’s server</a> for easier troubleshooting</li> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/sosparser">A tool which turns log files into interactive tables to easily sort and filter columns</a></li> <li>A functionality to<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/chatops/"> ChatOps</a> to make it easier to identify user accounts on GitLab.com</li> </ul> <p><strong>What you’ll do</strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">  </span></p> <ul> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Support a mix of Self-managed and GitLab.com (SaaS) customers and resolve their issues via Zendesk tickets, merge requests, email and video conferencing</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Collaborate with our </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/product/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Product</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">, </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/development/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Development</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">, </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/infrastructure/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Infrastructure</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">, </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-success/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Customer Success</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> and </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/sales/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Sales</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> Teams to build new features and fix bugs, define and shape the product goals, roadmap, priorities, and strategy</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Create and update documentation based on customer interactions</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Collaborate with Support team members (through </span><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/support-pairing/?_gl=1%2a1vj7usl%2a_ga%2aMTYyOTI0OTAxNC4xNjc4NzIwMDg0%2a_ga_ENFH3X7M5Y%2aMTY4NDgzNDU0OC4xMTAuMS4xNjg0ODM2NDM3LjAuMC4w"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Pairing Sessions</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">) and other GitLab team members (for example: as a </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/support/#support-stable-counterpart"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Support Stable Counterpart</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">)</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Participate in regular rotations for weekday and weekend on-call coverage (daytime only), providing emergency support to our Self-managed and SaaS customers, or working with our SaaS Production team to coordinate incident communications</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Participate in our hiring processes by reviewing applications and assessments, and by participating in interviews.</span></li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>What you’ll bring </strong></p> <ul> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Experience in, and passion for managing customer facing cases throughout the entire support lifecycle from initial customer inquiry to triage and reproduction, writing bug reports for hand off to the development team, and case resolution</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Excellent Linux systems administration knowledge (LFCE or RHCE equivalent knowledge)</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Ability to use scripting languages (preferably Ruby or Bash), and MVC frameworks (preferably Ruby on Rails)</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Experience with Git and CI/CD</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Expertise in writing support content </span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Ability to communicate complex technical topics to customers and coworkers of varying technical skill level</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Familiarity with DevOps methodologies and technologies like Serverless and Kubernetes</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Understand a range of different GitLab implementations, and how service interruptions impact the customer.</span></li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">The Support team is distributed all over the world across AMER, EMEA, and APAC regions. Support Engineers work on Support Tickets and helping GitLab’s customers, but they also dig into the code and logs to find out why something is not working as expected. The Collaboration here at GitLab is extraordinary and exciting - Support Engineers </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/support/workflows/how-to-get-help.html"><span style="font-weight: 400;">solve complex problems together</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> and participate in regular pairing sessions and 1:1s, as well as coffee chats and Slack conversations that help them stay connected. Team members are given the ability to structure their shift the way it best suits their private life while maintaining our ability to address customer issues. </span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Thanks to our </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/all-remote/values/#transparency"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Transparency</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> value, you can see what we are working on in our </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/support/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Support Team</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> page. Additionally, you can see our company </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/direction/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">roadmap</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> and </span><a href="https://www.youtube.com/@Gitlab"><span style="font-weight: 400;">listen</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> to some of our meetings. </span></p> <p> </p> <h4><strong>How GitLab will support you</strong></h4> <ul> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</span></a></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/all-remote/guide/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">All remote</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">, </span><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/all-remote/asynchronous/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">asynchronous</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> work environment</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/paid-time-off/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Flexible Paid Time Off</span></a></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/erg-guide/#:~:text=Definition%20of%20the%20TMRG%20%2D%20Team%20Member%20Resource%20Groups,-TMRGs%20are%20voluntary&text=The%20purpose%20for%20this%20type,developing%20the%20sense%20of%20belonging."><span style="font-weight: 400

You'll work with leaders across Product Management, Product Marketing, Finance, go-to-market teams, Sales, and Deal Desk to evaluate opportunities, create business models for new offerings, and competitor pricing, and customer and usage data to make evidence-based pricing recommendations.</li> <li>Use structured problem-solving to form hypotheses, complete analysis, validate findings, and recommend actions.</li> <li>Conduct regular pricing reviews, identify opportunities, and help create and carry out plans to address them.</li> <li>Evaluate new business models and monetization approaches as GitLab's portfolio evolves, especially for AI, credit-based pricing, and usage-based products.</li> <li>Partner with product and fulfillment teams to prioritize launches and map new stock keeping units (SKUs) to the correct products and feature sets.</li> <li>Monitor pricing and packaging changes after launch and apply what you learn to ongoing strategy.</li> <li>Communicate pricing concepts and recommendations clearly, influence senior leaders, and build alignment across stakeholders with competing priorities.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Significant experience leading software as a service (SaaS) pricing strategy and analysis across products or a complex portfolio.</li> <li>Experience with financial analysis and modeling, with the ability to use data and business intelligence tools such as Sisense or Tableau to support recommendations.</li> <li>Strong analytical skills and the ability to turn complex data into clear, practical communication skills, with experience presenting to and influencing senior stakeholders and collaborating with Legal, FP&A, Investor Relations, and business partners.</li> <li>Proficiency with Workiva Wdesk and NetSuite is preferred.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Accounting team supports accurate, timely, and transparent financial reporting at GitLab.
